rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly, so this table pushes strength up while protecting the one thing that dominates this benchmark: the FloatMM/IntMM/RealMM matrix-multiply inner loops, which execute many iterations and make bogus-control-flow and indirect-branch overhead multiply quickly. SUB gets the highest weights across the board because instruction substitution is nearly free at runtime, small in code size, and very hard to get wrong, making it the best strength-per-cost pass for a tiny 849-byte text image; FLA and SPLIT stay moderately aggressive since flattening plus splitting hides the simple nested-loop control-flow structure of the matrix kernels without per-iteration cost. BCF and IBR are kept valuable for security but with deliberately low runtime tolerances (0.4) so the scheduler steers them away from the hot numeric loops and toward cold functions like the various initializers and Oscar/Towers/Queens routines; ICALL is capped hard (runtime 0.3, risk 0.5) because this program has very few indirect-call candidates and converting calls in a 7-function image adds pointer-analysis friction for a reverse engineer but real size and mis-speculation cost; IGV sits at neutral moderate values as a low-risk diversity add-on across the benchmark's many small interrelated routines. Size tolerances mirror runtime tolerances since the binary is tiny and BCF-style duplication would bloat it disproportionately, and all correctness-risk tolerances are held at or above 0.5 to preserve the clean round-1 correctness result.
